in_favor.quote: It would be our intention to assure that the costs that we incur in providing temporary Olympic service will be recovered from those who use the temporary Olympic services; that is, the Olympic Committee, press agencies, broadcasters, timing company, computer company, etc.

in_favor.quote: Our grantee, CEI of Essex County, has proven its worth as the actual operator of the Bobrun, and it is our recommendation, and indeed our assumption, that CFI will continue to fulfill this function during pre and post-Olympic periods.

in_favor.role: governing body of the Olympic Games

conditional.role: Chief, Environmental Impacts Branch, EPA Region II
conditional.quote: It is our determination that the proposals will have acceptable impacts on air and water quality and, therefore, we have no objections to the project as proposed. Several questions, however, remain outstanding before we can complete our review, primarily in the area of water supply.

conditional.role: Director, Office of Environmental Affairs, HEW
conditional.quote: From the standpoint of the concerns of this Department, we feel it is a well prepared statement.

conditional.entity: Department of Health, Education, and Welfare
conditional.quote: Our only comment on the draft is in respect to the sanitary inspection system. We feel there is a need for sanitary inspection both during the games and the off-season period. This provision should be included in the final EIS.

the FAA has issued a finding of "not hazardous to navigation" relative to the presence at Intervale of the twin ski jump towers. This finding is conditional on FAA approved aircraft warning lights for the towers and has been confirmed by the Lake Placid Airport Manager.

FAA has made a "Determination of No Hazard to Air Navigation," subject to the condition that the tower will be top-lighted with a red beacon and that FAA is informed not less than 90 days from the start of construction so that optional traffic patterns may be implemented.
Our recommendation, therefore, is that EDA ensure that a combination of union and non-union labor be secured by establishing such requirements prior to the awarding of contracts.

We feel this environmental impact statement can be made adequate in its final form by inclusion and discussion of favorable commentaries from the State Historic Preservation Officer and the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation, by inclusion of a qualified archeologist's outlook on the probability of effect of the project on archeological values, and finally the display of a contingency plan for the protection of cultural resources during construction if any such values overlooked now become evident then.
